execution.validation: Telemetry comes from the exact packaged build and repeatable scenario; generated/display frames are not substituted for native simulation/render evidence.

execution.deliverable: Reproducibility evidence bundle and index.
execution.objective: Assemble a minimal chain from exact source to clean build to clean-machine play so an outside technical reviewer can reproduce the claim.
execution.required_evidence: Evidence index, digests, Git commit/tree, Drive readback.
execution.validation: Every link source -> build -> package -> install -> play -> persistence -> diagnostics is backed by exact identities; missing proof remains explicitly unresolved.

execution.deliverable: Canonical slice scenario definition with start state, route, combat/system beats, end state, and exact build identity.
execution.objective: Choose a 10-20 minute representative sequence only from implemented, accepted gameplay and content; do not invent a mechanic to make the demo more cinematic.
execution.required_evidence: Scenario file, package identity, first raw run capture.
execution.validation: Scenario can be executed in the packaged game and demonstrates the project's real player+rival+infected+arena interaction without scripted substitution.

execution.deliverable: Traversal/camera issue record plus accepted run evidence after task-scoped fixes if required.
execution.objective: Evaluate player locomotion, camera behavior, collision, readability, and spatial navigation in raw gameplay.
execution.required_evidence: Raw capture, runtime log, exact changed source if repaired.
execution.validation: The canonical route is playable without camera clipping, collision traps, navigation ambiguity that blocks intended play, or noninteractive presentation substitutions.

execution.deliverable: Combat-quality evidence and bounded repair changes where current behavior fails acceptance.
execution.objective: Exercise real input -> weapon/action -> hit resolution -> damage -> reaction -> state change during the canonical slice.
execution.required_evidence: Raw combat capture, telemetry/log events, source/build identity.
execution.validation: Combat actions are responsive and legible, consequences are real simulation state, and no visual-only effect is counted as gameplay completion.

tasks.title: Prove combat feel and consequence chain

execution.deliverable: System-interaction evidence trace and raw gameplay capture.
execution.objective: Capture at least one genuine interaction where player, rival, infected, and approved arena pressure all affect the same evolving encounter.
execution.required_evidence: Event timeline, raw video, runtime logs, package digest.
execution.validation: Actor decisions and world consequences originate from runtime state; the encounter is not a prerecorded or manually staged substitute for implementation.

tasks.title: Prove player, rival, infected, and arena interaction

execution.deliverable: Animation-quality defect list reduced to accepted slice quality, with exact repaired assets/source where needed.
execution.objective: Inspect locomotion, aim, weapon handling, hit/death reactions, transitions, deformation, and motion continuity at gameplay distance.
execution.required_evidence: Raw captures at representative moments, source/asset identities, runtime evidence.
execution.validation: No acceptance-blocking snapping, foot sliding, broken deformation, impossible pose transitions, or actor-state mismatch remains in the slice.

execution.deliverable: Readability evidence and task-scoped fixes to existing implemented feedback.
execution.objective: Verify event-driven audio/VFX/UI communicate real gameplay state without obscuring targets, routes, hazards, or decisions.
execution.required_evidence: Raw capture with audio, HUD/state event trace, exact source/asset identities.
execution.validation: Critical events are perceptible and attributable; UI/VFX/audio do not claim mechanics absent from runtime state and do not block gameplay readability.

tasks.title: Qualify audio, VFX, HUD, and gameplay readability

execution.deliverable: Environment-quality evidence and bounded corrections within accepted project visual direction.
execution.objective: Evaluate the canonical slice environment as a playable production space: geometry, scale, materials, lighting, props, collision, navigation, and damage/state coherence.
execution.required_evidence: Raw traversal/combat captures, map/asset identities, runtime logs.
execution.validation: No acceptance-blocking floating/fused geometry, impossible access, contradictory scale/perspective, unreadable route, material failure, or unexplained world-state artifact remains.

tasks.title: Qualify environment, material, lighting, and world coherence

execution.deliverable: Indexed slice bundle containing exact build, scenario, raw full run, selected excerpts, metrics, known limitations, and source identities.
execution.objective: Package the canonical slice proof without editing raw gameplay into evidence that hides runtime defects.
execution.required_evidence: Bundle digest/index, Git commit/tree, Drive readback.
execution.validation: A reviewer can trace every claimed visual/gameplay quality point to the exact running build and raw evidence; unresolved defects are disclosed.

execution.deliverable: Consent-aware playtest protocol and telemetry/question set limited to product evaluation.
execution.objective: Define what an external player receives, what founder help is prohibited during the session, what evidence is collected, and what counts as completion/failure.
execution.required_evidence: Protocol file and test package identity.
execution.validation: Protocol can be run without exposing internal secrets or requiring founder coaching; success criteria derive from the playable product rather than investor narrative.

execution.deliverable: External playtest handoff bundle.
execution.objective: Create the smallest package, instructions, and issue-report path needed for an outside player to install, launch, play, and report results.
execution.required_evidence: Bundle digest, clean-machine dry run, instructions readback.
execution.validation: A person not using the development workspace can follow the instructions without hidden commands or direct founder intervention.

execution.deliverable: Session record with launch outcome, completion path, blockers, comprehension issues, crashes, and opt-in qualitative feedback.
execution.objective: Observe one real external player using the packaged build under the blind protocol.
execution.required_evidence: Session ID, build digest, telemetry/logs, consented notes/captures.
execution.validation: Session evidence comes from the participant's real play; founder assistance is recorded rather than hidden; failures remain failures.

execution.deliverable: Second independent session record and environment comparison.
execution.objective: Repeat external play on a materially different machine/user context to expose founder-machine assumptions.
execution.required_evidence: Machine profile, session result, logs, build identity.
execution.validation: The same package/handoff path is used; machine-specific failures are isolated rather than changing the product story.

tasks.title: Run independent session on a different machine context

execution.deliverable: Evidence-linked playtest findings ranked by reproducibility and impact on intended play.
execution.objective: Convert observed external-session facts into a prioritized defect/clarity set without turning subjective comments into fabricated metrics.
execution.required_evidence: Finding index with session references.
execution.validation: Every finding links to an observed session event or explicit participant feedback; no unsupported generalization is presented as player consensus.

tasks.title: Aggregate external comprehension and friction evidence

execution.deliverable: Task-scoped source/content changes plus focused regression evidence.
execution.objective: Fix only product defects clearly evidenced by external sessions and revalidate their affected boundaries.
execution.required_evidence: Before/after evidence, commit/tree, new package identity.
execution.validation: Each fixed blocker is reproduced before repair where possible, no longer reproduces after repair, and unaffected verified behavior is preserved.

execution.deliverable: Post-repair session evidence.
execution.objective: Give the repaired package to an external player and repeat the affected scenario without founder steering.
execution.required_evidence: Session logs/captures, package digest, comparison to prior findings.
execution.validation: Previously targeted blockers are no longer acceptance-blocking; new failures are recorded without expanding the task into unrelated redesign.

execution.deliverable: Independent-player proof bundle with exact session/build identities and bounded qualitative/quantitative findings.
execution.objective: Assemble external-play evidence sufficient to demonstrate the game can be installed, understood, and played beyond the founder environment.
execution.required_evidence: Bundle index/digest, session references, Drive readback.
execution.validation: Bundle distinguishes observed facts, participant statements, and interpretation; no claim of broad market validation is made from a small cohort.

execution.deliverable: Updated technical decision entries for measured target hardware tiers or explicit retained UNKNOWNs where evidence is insufficient.
execution.objective: Use packaged-runtime telemetry and accepted product intent to replace only the hardware-tier UNKNOWNs that can now be decided.
execution.required_evidence: Decision diff, telemetry source IDs, commit/tree.
execution.validation: Each accepted value has measured evidence and owner/delegated authority; no GPU/RAM/VRAM target is inferred from installed hardware alone.

tasks.title: Lock representative target hardware tiers from measured evidence

execution.deliverable: Updated performance decision entries and repeatable benchmark scenarios.
execution.objective: Define target native FPS/frame-time/hitch/latency tiers only where representative measurements support a production decision.
execution.required_evidence: Decision record, benchmark telemetry, source commit.
execution.validation: Targets exclude generated frames as native performance and are tied to accepted hardware/scenario identities.

tasks.title: Lock native frame-time and responsiveness targets from evidence

execution.deliverable: Traversal stress evidence and bounded fixes.
execution.objective: Run representative high-motion traversal through streamed world boundaries and repair acceptance-blocking stalls or continuity defects.
execution.required_evidence: Frame-time trace, streaming logs, raw capture, build digest.
execution.validation: Streaming, HLOD/culling/occlusion, collision, and world-state continuity remain valid through the scenario within accepted performance targets.

tasks.title: Qualify world traversal streaming and hitch behavior

execution.deliverable: Combat stress profile and bounded optimization changes if required.
execution.objective: Run representative simultaneous player/rival/infected combat at the population level supported by current content and measure degradation.
execution.required_evidence: Actor/event counts, CPU/GPU/frame telemetry, runtime logs.
execution.validation: Simulation correctness and gameplay readability remain intact at the accepted scenario load; counts are evidence-driven rather than ambition-driven.

execution.deliverable: Resource qualification record and leak/residency fixes where evidenced.
execution.objective: Measure resource residency through traversal, combat, restart, and repeated scenario execution.
execution.required_evidence: Resource traces, lifecycle logs, build/source identity.
execution.validation: RAM/VRAM/resource use is bounded for accepted scenarios and does not grow materially from lifecycle defects across repeated runs.

tasks.title: Qualify memory, VRAM, residency, and leak behavior

execution.deliverable: Stability run evidence plus repaired failures limited to reproduced issues.
execution.objective: Run the accepted representative soak/repetition duration chosen from current release risk and capture crashes, hangs, asserts, and state degradation.
execution.required_evidence: Runtime logs, duration/scenario record, crash/assert artifacts if any.
execution.validation: The exact packaged build survives the accepted duration/repetition scenario without unresolved release-blocking failure.

execution.deliverable: Shipping package with exact source/build identity and clean-machine play evidence.
execution.objective: Produce and validate the accepted Win64 Shipping configuration after performance/stability repairs.
execution.required_evidence: Shipping package digest, runtime logs, raw play capture.
execution.validation: Package launches outside editor, completes the canonical slice, persists required state, and exits/relaunches cleanly on the qualified environment.

execution.deliverable: Release-operations qualification bundle.
execution.objective: Assemble current build, performance, stability, persistence, diagnostics, update, and clean-machine results into one release-operations evidence set.
execution.required_evidence: Bundle index/digest, Git source identity, Drive readback.
execution.validation: Every accepted release claim points to fresh exact-build evidence; stale predecessor logs are references only.

execution.deliverable: Second-scenario production brief with reuse targets, required variation, and acceptance scenario.
execution.objective: Choose a materially different scenario that reuses existing systems and approved content vocabulary rather than introducing a new project identity.
execution.required_evidence: Brief, source/asset references, acceptance route.
execution.validation: Scenario is distinct enough to test repeatability but remains within accepted mechanics, art direction, and current project scope.

tasks.title: Select second production scenario from current accepted systems

execution.deliverable: Editable scenario content integrated in the game.
execution.objective: Build the second scenario using existing modular world/content systems before adding bespoke logic.
execution.required_evidence: Source/asset diff, runtime traversal evidence.
execution.validation: Scenario is playable, collision/navigation-valid, and reuses production systems; bespoke code is justified by an actual missing universal/project capability.

tasks.title: Produce second environment or encounter composition through reusable systems

execution.deliverable: Second encounter composition and runtime evidence.
execution.objective: Use existing actor/system definitions to create a meaningfully different interaction pattern without forking core AI behavior per encounter.
execution.required_evidence: Encounter data/source identity, raw gameplay/event trace.
execution.validation: Rival/infected behavior remains driven by shared systems and current approved tuning/content data, with real state interaction.

tasks.title: Produce different rival and infected encounter composition

execution.deliverable: Second pressure sequence integrated into scenario data/world state.
execution.objective: Recombine the already approved arena-pressure mechanism with the second scenario without inventing a new pressure mechanic.
execution.required_evidence: State/event trace, scenario source, runtime capture.
execution.validation: The same authoritative pressure system drives different valid consequences; no duplicate pressure controller is created.

tasks.title: Produce alternate arena-pressure sequence from current accepted systems

execution.deliverable: Reuse report tied to source diffs and production task evidence.
execution.objective: Quantify which second-scenario outputs were achieved through reusable data/assets/systems and which required new implementation.
execution.required_evidence: Git diff stats, task/run identities, categorized reuse record.
execution.validation: Counts/times come from real changed files/tasks/traces; no claim of reuse is based only on architecture intent.

tasks.title: Measure content-system reuse versus bespoke work

execution.deliverable: Second-scenario packaged proof.
execution.objective: Build a package containing the second scenario and execute its representative route outside the editor.
execution.required_evidence: Package digest, raw gameplay, runtime logs.
execution.validation: Clean launch and real play succeed with the same release pipeline and evidence standards used for the canonical slice.

execution.deliverable: Repeatability comparison with elapsed production time, accepted-task count, founder interventions, changed source/assets, and validation outcome where observable.
execution.objective: Compare first- and second-scenario creation using actual task/run timelines and acceptance evidence.
execution.required_evidence: Trace IDs, calculation inputs, comparison report.
execution.validation: Metrics are computed from durable traces and comparable task boundaries; missing telemetry is marked unknown rather than estimated.

tasks.title: Compare production time, intervention, and quality across scenarios

execution.deliverable: Repeatable-content evidence bundle linking both scenarios and their production traces.
execution.objective: Demonstrate that the playable quality pipeline can produce more than one strong scenario without rebuilding the game architecture each time.
execution.required_evidence: Bundle index/digest, source identities, Drive readback.
execution.validation: Both scenarios run in qualified packages, share core systems, and have evidence-linked production metrics; one-off bespoke hero work is separated from reusable capability.

execution.deliverable: Versioned evidence schema for tasks, runs, accepted outcomes, founder interventions, elapsed time, model/provider/resource use, cost where available, and recovery events.
execution.objective: Define the minimal durable measurements needed to quantify AI-native execution leverage without creating a second analytics authority or leaking project-private content.
execution.required_evidence: Schema/source commit and mapping to current Engine interfaces.
execution.validation: Schema maps to current Engine Task/Run/Resource/Event concepts or existing semantic equivalents; it does not create project-specific permanent Engine types.

execution.deliverable: Throughput dataset/report with task IDs, acceptance state, period boundaries, and source traces.
execution.objective: Calculate accepted production-task throughput for bounded periods using durable execution records rather than chat estimates.
execution.required_evidence: Task/run IDs, calculation script/query if needed, resulting dataset digest.
execution.validation: Every counted task has durable accepted completion evidence; retries and failed attempts are not miscounted as accepted output.

tasks.title: Compute accepted-task throughput from real traces

execution.deliverable: Intervention dataset with explicit categories and links to source events.
execution.objective: Classify real founder interventions needed to redirect, repair, decide, or accept work and measure them against accepted outputs.
execution.required_evidence: Event/task references and aggregate calculation.
execution.validation: Only observed interventions are counted; authority/acceptance actions are not mislabeled as engineering labor without evidence.

tasks.title: Measure founder intervention per accepted outcome

execution.deliverable: Cost/resource dataset and normalized per-outcome view where source data exists.
execution.objective: Aggregate available real usage/cost evidence by accepted task or milestone while preserving provider/resource replaceability.
execution.required_evidence: Resource/event records, provider invoices/usage references where authorized, calculation output.
execution.validation: Costs are from provider/runtime records or exact measured resource use; unavailable prices are UNKNOWN rather than fabricated.

tasks.title: Measure compute, model, tool, and infrastructure cost per outcome

execution.deliverable: Cycle-time dataset across selected Games and Engine tasks.
execution.objective: Measure elapsed time from durable objective/task activation through validated output for representative tasks.
execution.required_evidence: Task/run/event IDs and calculation output.
execution.validation: Start/end boundaries are defined from actual persisted Task/Run/Event states; paused or externally blocked time is distinguishable where evidence supports it.

execution.deliverable: Recovery benchmark record.
execution.objective: Interrupt a representative active workload at an accepted safe boundary and verify continuation from durable state without replaying verified completed work.
execution.required_evidence: Pre-interruption state identity, restart evidence, post-recovery task/run IDs.
execution.validation: A new process/session/resource reconstructs current task state and continues correctly; unaffected verified outputs remain reused.

execution.deliverable: Cross-model/provider continuity benchmark.
execution.objective: Continue one representative project objective across a model/provider change without changing project truth or task semantics merely to fit the worker.
execution.required_evidence: Before/after worker/resource identities, task/run evidence, output validation.
execution.validation: The replacement worker receives durable current project/task state, preserves accepted work, and completes the next bounded output with normal task-derived validation.

tasks.title: Benchmark model or provider continuity on the same project

execution.deliverable: Founder-leverage report with calculations and exact trace references.
execution.objective: Assemble measured throughput, intervention, cycle time, resource cost, recovery, and continuity evidence into a reproducible report.
execution.required_evidence: Report digest, calculation inputs, Engine source/trace identities, Drive publication readback.
execution.validation: Every number can be recomputed from cited durable evidence; unsupported narrative claims are omitted.

execution.deliverable: Pilot brief with owner/user objective, project boundary, allowed resources, expected output contract, and acceptance evidence.
execution.objective: Bind one real outside-user/project objective that tests Biella as a universal execution system rather than a game-specific automation.
execution.required_evidence: Pilot brief, project identity, accepted output contract.
execution.validation: Pilot does not import Biella Games canon into Engine behavior and does not depend on MiniTZ historical instructions.

execution.deliverable: External deployment/onboarding package tied to an exact Engine commit.
execution.objective: Reduce current Engine deployment/onboarding to a reproducible package or documented procedure that does not require reconstructing the founder environment by hand.
execution.required_evidence: Engine commit/tree, deployment logs, environment identity.
execution.validation: A fresh authorized environment can instantiate the required Engine services/state using the package without undocumented founder-only repair.

tasks.title: Package repeatable external deployment and onboarding path

execution.deliverable: Pilot project/task identities and onboarding evidence.
execution.objective: Have the external pilot user/environment establish its project and first task through the supported interface rather than by editing internal Engine state.
execution.required_evidence: Project/task IDs, interface logs, persisted state readback.
execution.validation: Required project truth and task contract are persisted through supported Engine boundaries; manual database/file surgery is not part of the normal path.

tasks.title: Onboard external pilot without founder reconstruction

execution.deliverable: Validated pilot artifact and execution trace.
execution.objective: Run the pilot objective through real resources and produce the contracted output with task-derived validation.
execution.required_evidence: Artifact identity/digest, run/events, validation evidence.
execution.validation: Artifact matches the pilot output contract and is linked to exact Task/Run/Graph/source/resource identities; agent claim alone is insufficient.

tasks.title: Execute first external objective to a validated artifact

execution.deliverable: External pilot continuation record.
execution.objective: End the active process/session and prove the external project can be reconstructed from durable state.
execution.required_evidence: Shutdown/restart evidence, persisted object identities, reconstructed state readback.
execution.validation: Project/task/run state reappears correctly without relying on chat context, RAM, temporary cache, or founder memory.

tasks.title: Persist and reconstruct external pilot state

execution.deliverable: External recovery benchmark.
execution.objective: Introduce or use a real bounded interruption and verify smallest-boundary recovery.
execution.required_evidence: Failure evidence, recovery actions, resulting task/run/artifact identities.
execution.validation: Only invalidated work is retried; verified unaffected artifacts/state are preserved; continuation reaches the same project truth.

tasks.title: Recover pilot after bounded infrastructure interruption

execution.deliverable: Second validated pilot output linked to the same durable project.
execution.objective: Demonstrate that the pilot is a continuing project rather than a one-shot demo by completing a next bounded objective, optionally using a different worker/provider where appropriate.
execution.required_evidence: Second task/run/artifact identities and validation.
execution.validation: Project truth and prior accepted artifacts remain stable; new work is a new task/run rather than mutation of historical evidence.

tasks.title: Continue external pilot with second objective or worker change

execution.deliverable: External replication evidence bundle.
execution.objective: Assemble onboarding, execution, persistence, recovery, and continuation evidence showing the founder's leverage transfers to another project/user environment.
execution.required_evidence: Bundle index/digest, pilot references, Drive readback.
execution.validation: Bundle is reproducible from exact Engine/source/deployment identities and clearly separates pilot user outcomes from founder-run internal proof.

execution.deliverable: Public proof page or media package with raw-gameplay provenance and exact build/source references kept internally.
execution.objective: Prepare and publish a public-facing proof surface using only accepted build facts and gameplay evidence; no invented title/release date/platform promise or fake gameplay.
execution.required_evidence: Published URL/identity, source media digest, internal evidence mapping.
execution.validation: Published material matches the running product and does not present generated concepts or cinematics as implemented gameplay.

execution.deliverable: External distribution record and downloadable/installable build identity.
execution.objective: Use an accepted distribution mechanism to deliver the exact qualified build to external testers without requiring development-workspace access.
execution.required_evidence: Distribution artifact ID, package digest, tester delivery records without unnecessary personal data.
execution.validation: Recipients receive the exact intended package, install/launch succeeds under the qualified instructions, and distribution identity is read back.

tasks.title: Distribute qualified build to bounded external test cohort

execution.deliverable: Demand-signal dataset with source, timestamp, and definition for each metric.
execution.objective: Collect only actual opt-in signals available on the accepted distribution/public surface, such as test requests, followers, wishlists if a store is accepted, or qualified inbound interest.
execution.required_evidence: Export/readback from demand source and dataset digest.
execution.validation: Every metric comes from a real platform/source record; platform-specific metrics are not invented when that platform is not active.

tasks.title: Capture real demand signals from proof surface

execution.deliverable: Game demand report with exact source counts, dates, cohort definitions, and limitations.
execution.objective: Summarize external play participation and demand signals without extrapolating unsupported market size or conversion claims.
execution.required_evidence: Report digest and underlying source identities.
execution.validation: Reported totals reconcile to source exports/readbacks; duplicates and unverified anecdotes are excluded or clearly separated.

execution.deliverable: Commercial pilot/pricing package describing scope, usage basis, support boundary, deliverables, and exclusions.
execution.objective: Turn the proven external Engine pilot capability into a clear bounded paid offer or recurring pricing model without changing Engine architecture to fit a sales document.
execution.required_evidence: Offer document identity, capability/evidence references.
execution.validation: Offer maps to capabilities actually proven by external replication; unimplemented enterprise features are not promised.
